Allowed: public domain or CC0, and OFL for fonts (docs/templates.md).

credit.title: Under the Wave off Kanagawa (Kanagawa oki nami ura), also known as The Great Wave, from the series Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji
credit.creator: Katsushika Hokusai (1760–1849)
credit.source: The Metropolitan Museum of Art (accession JP1847, H. O. Havemeyer Collection, Bequest of Mrs. H. O. Havemeyer, 1929)

assets.notes: The Great Wave, Met JP1847, woodblock print, 3859x2594, the vivid edge-to-edge impression (saturated Prussian blue, warm cream sky, no paper margin). Keep whole: default fit inside 1920x1080 leaves thin side bars (aspect 1.49). Composition: wave claw top-left/centre, Fuji small at lower centre-right, open cream sky upper right for a wall label if overlaid. Met Open Access CC0 (isPublicDomain true via API). AIC copies were blocked by a Cloudflare challenge for plain curl, so the Met is used.

assets.name: Under the Wave off Kanagawa (detail 1) — Katsushika Hokusai (The Met, CC0).webp

credit.source: The Metropolitan Museum of Art (accession JP1847, H. O. Havemeyer Collection, Bequest of Mrs. H. O. Havemeyer, 1929)

assets.notes: The great claw: the curling crest and its finger-like foam talons breaking left to right, with deep-blue wave body on the left edge and a wide band of empty cream sky to the right (good for a caption on the right third). Same source file as 'wave'; crop checked by rendering with ffmpeg.

assets.name: Under the Wave off Kanagawa (detail 2) — Katsushika Hokusai (The Met, CC0).webp

assets.name: Under the Wave off Kanagawa (detail 3) — Katsushika Hokusai (The Met, CC0).webp

assets.name: Ocean surface waves — Mostafameraji (Wikimedia Commons, CC0).mp4
assets.notes: 1920x1080 25 fps Theora, 20.0 s, locked-off telephoto of open sea: rows of small teal-blue swells with white crests rolling in, no horizon, no shore, no people, no text, no cuts (scene-detect clean). Calm, even, steady; loops well with a 1 s crossfade. Colour is cool teal-grey, sits well beside the prints. NOTE: not PD-government footage; it is the uploader's own work released CC0 on Commons (verified LicenseShortName=CC0 via API). Commons was rate-limiting (HTTP 429) late in the session; the URL is the stable original.

assets.name: Sea Waves — Joseph Sardin (BigSoundBank, CC0).m4a
assets.notes: 48 kHz 16-bit stereo XY field recording (Tascam DR-40), 2:47, realistic seaside soundscape: continuous surf with gentle wave-break swells every few seconds. Very steady (integrated -15 LUFS, LRA 4.4 LU); spectrogram shows no birds, voices or engines. A 60 s excerpt from 0:20 loops cleanly with the fades. The page states CC0 (public-domain equivalent), no attribution required. Commons PD candidates were weaker (a 2003 MiniDisc beach clip; a pebble-beach clip with a motorboat and footsteps).

assets.name: ISS Timelapse: West Coast of the Americas — NASA (SVS, PD).mp4

credit.title: ISS Timelapse: West Coast of the Americas (Expedition 28 night pass, 19 Aug 2011)
credit.creator: NASA / ISS Expedition 28 crew; NASA Goddard SVS
credit.basis: US government work (NASA); no NASA logo or insignia in the frames used

assets.notes: Night time-lapse from the ISS over the Pacific coast of North America: amber city lights streaming past under moonlit cloud, thin orange airglow line on the limb, stars above, an ISS solar array in the upper-right corner. 4096x2304 30 fps (exact 16:9; scaled to 1920x1080), 54.7 s, no text/logos, no cuts. The file is large (~735 MB); the 720p version is too small for the brief. Grade cools the shadows to navy and nudges mids toward violet while keeping the city lights warm; checked on a rendered frame, not crushed.

assets.name: Solar Prominence Dance — NASA SDO (SVS, PD).mp4

credit.title: Solar Prominence Dance - December 31, 2012 (SDO/AIA 304 Å)
credit.creator: NASA/SDO (AIA); NASA Goddard SVS
credit.basis: US government work (NASA); no NASA logo or insignia in the frames used

assets.notes: Full solar disk in 304 Å extreme ultraviolet from SDO: a churning, granular fiery surface with bright active regions and a twisting prominence on the left limb, slowly evolving over 40 s, no cuts. The source has a small date stamp in the lower-left; the crop (1560x878 from x180,y100) removes it and enlarges the disk to fill the frame height (disk fully inside, checked). Grade rotates hue -30° so the orange becomes hot magenta-red and lifts the black space to a deep navy. NASA-only (SDO).

assets.name: Milky Way Zoom — NASA Goddard (SVS, PD).mp4

credit.title: The Heliosphere Within The Milky Way Galaxy — MilkyWayZoom (with stars)
credit.creator: NASA Goddard Space Flight Center (visualization: Adriana Manrique Gutierrez; producer: Joy Ng)
credit.basis: US government work (NASA); no NASA logo or insignia in the frames used

assets.notes: Slow, smooth push-in on a face-on spiral galaxy (artist's rendering of the Milky Way, NASA Goddard CGI) from a small spiral on black into its glowing core and dusty star-flecked arms; 20 s, no text, no cuts. File is actually 3840x2160 despite the '1080' name; scaled down. Grade gives the black a deep indigo cast and the arms a violet tint without crushing the core. Credits are NASA Goddard staff only (no ESA/Hubble/Webb material). The loop jumps from close-in back to wide at the seam, hence the 1.5 s crossfade.

assets.name: ISS Timelapse: Aurora Australis — NASA (SVS, PD).mp4

credit.title: ISS Timelapse: Aurora Australis (Expedition 29, 17 Sep 2011)
credit.creator: NASA / ISS Expedition 29 crew; NASA Goddard SVS
credit.basis: US government work (NASA); no NASA logo or insignia in the frames used

assets.notes: Dramatic time-lapse from the ISS over the Indian Ocean: rivers of aurora light flowing over Earth with a red upper fringe and stars; ISS solar array (right) and module (top) frame the shot. 4096x2304 30 fps, 45.8 s, no text/logos, no cuts; the aurora is strongest in the first ~25 s, so the excerpt is 1–19 s. The grade is a strong recolour: a channel mix that turns the natural green aurora violet-blue and magenta with a red-violet top fringe (checked on a rendered frame, highlights intact). For natural green, use 'eq=contrast=1.08:saturation=1.25,colorbalance=bs=0.08:rs=0.06' instead. ~255 MB file.

assets.name: Ambiant Shock — Komiku (Wikimedia Commons, CC0).m4a
assets.notes: Instrumental ambient piece, 2:44, by Komiku, who wrote and recorded it and released it CC0 (so both composition and recording are CC0; Commons LicenseShortName=CC0). From the spectrogram the first ~90 s are sustained, evolving pads with no percussive hits; pulsing elements arrive after ~1:30, hence the 0–90 s excerpt. Quiet master (-17.7 LUFS), so it may need gain. NOT auditioned by ear (checked only by spectrogram and loudness), so give it a listen; if it is not dark enough, John Bartmann 'dark-dyne' (CC0, Commons) is the fallback. upload.wikimedia.org returned HTTP 429 to direct downloads during this session; analysis used the Commons MP3 transcode https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/transcoded/c/c7/Komiku_-_05_-_Ambiant_Shock.ogg/Komiku_-_05_-_Ambiant_Shock.ogg.mp3, and the original URL above is stable once the limit clears.

assets.name: I Do Like to Be Beside the Seaside — Arthur Norton (Harry Fay), Zonophone 1909 (Internet Archive, PD).m4a

credit.title: I Do Like to Be Beside the Seaside
credit.creator: John A. Glover-Kind (words and music); sung by Arthur Norton (pseudonym of Harry Fay)
credit.basis: Song published 1907; Glover-Kind died 1918. Recording published 1909 (Zonophone X-42943); in the US, sound recordings published before 1923 entered the public domain on 1 Jan 2022 (Music Modernization Act), and UK recording rights expired long ago

assets.notes: Whole song, 194 s, mono acoustic 78 transfer (128 kbps MP3). A male music-hall singer with orchestra, period-authentic and easy to sing along to, but with steady surface hiss/swish all the way through (the uploader says the disc is worn). A gentle clean-up would help if the pipeline allows it, e.g. af 'highpass=f=90,lowpass=f=5500,afftdn=nf=-25'. The 1909 Mark Sheridan original could not be found anywhere with a clear PD/CC0 status. Lyrics are from the published 1907 song, transcribed on English Wikipedia (I could not check them against a scan of the 1907 sheet music). The recording may not sing every verse.
assets.lyrics:
Everyone delights to spend their summer's holiday
Down beside the side of the silvery sea.
I'm no exception to the rule, in fact, if I'd my way,
I'd reside by the side of the silvery sea.
But when you're just the common garden Smith or Jones or Brown,
At business up in town, you've got to settle down.
You save up all the money you can till summer comes around,
Then away you go to a spot you know where the cockleshells are found.

Chorus:
Oh! I do like to be beside the seaside!
I do like to be beside the sea!
Oh I do like to stroll along the Prom, Prom, Prom!
Where the brass bands play, "Tiddely-om-pom-pom!"
So just let me be beside the seaside!
I'll be beside myself with glee,
And there's lots of girls beside,
I should like to be beside, beside the seaside,
Beside the sea!

Timothy went to Blackpool for the day last Eastertide
To see what he could see by the side of the sea.
As soon as he reached the station there the first thing he espied
Was the wine lodge door stood open invitingly.
To quench his thirst, he toddled inside and called out for a wine,
Which grew to eight or nine, till his nose began to shine.
Said he, "What people see in the sea, I'm sure I fail to see,"
Then he caught the train back home again and to his wife said he:

(Chorus)

William Sykes the burglar, he'd been out to work one night,
Filled his bags with jewels, cash and plate.
Constable Brown felt quite surprised when William hove in sight.
Said he, "The hours you're keeping are far too late."
So he grabbed him by the collar and lodged him safe and sound in jail.
Next morning, looking pale, Bill told a tearful tale.
The judge said, "For a couple of months I'm sending you away!"
Said Bill, "How kind! Well, if you don't mind, where I spend my holiday!"

Oh! I do like to be beside the seaside!
I do like to be beside the sea!
For the sun's always shining as I make my way,
And the brass bands play, "Ta-ra-ra-boom-de-ay!"
So just let me be beside the seaside!
I'll be beside myself with glee,
And there's lots of girls beside,
I should like to be beside, beside the seaside,
Beside the sea!

assets.name: Clair de lune — Claude Debussy, Wright Brass of the US Air Force Band of Flight (Wikimedia Commons, PD).m4a

credit.title: Clair de lune (Suite bergamasque)
credit.creator: Claude Debussy; performed by Wright Brass, United States Air Force Band of Flight
credit.source: Wikimedia Commons (from music.af.mil Public Domain Music)
credit.basis: Composition: Debussy died 1918. Performance and recording: US government work by the United States Air Force Band (PD-USGov-Military-Air Force)

assets.notes: Brass-quintet arrangement, soft and warm, 242 s in total. The excerpt runs 0.7–157.7 s and ends at a natural pause (silence at 157.9 s), with a 5 s fade. Quiet master (please normalise). I rejected the Commons piano recording by Laurens Goedhart, which is CC BY 3.0 despite being labelled PD, and the 1927 Edison 'Hotel Commodore Ensemble' disc, which is not yet PD in the US (1927 recordings enter the PD on 1 Jan 2028).

assets.name: Waves on the shore — Dsw4 (Wikimedia Commons, PD).m4a

credit.title: Waves
credit.creator: Dsw4 (Wikimedia Commons user)
credit.basis: Released into the public domain by the recordist ({{PD-self}}) on Wikimedia Commons

assets.notes: Stereo field recording of small waves washing in on a shore, recorded with a shotgun microphone, 287 s in total. The 10–55 s excerpt is steady and gentle (about -22 LUFS), with no voices or engines. Caveat: it was recorded on the shore of Lake Ontario, not the sea, though it sounds like gentle surf. A sea-shore alternative: 'On a pebble beach' (earthcalling, PD via pdsounds.org, 40 s) https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/7/73/On_a_pebble_beach.ogg, but it includes a thrown stone, footsteps on pebbles and a distant motor boat. I rejected 'Ocean Waves on a Tropical Beach' (CC0) because the uploader and the credited author do not match.

assets.name: Sunset on the Sea — John Frederick Kensett (The Met, CC0).webp
assets.notes: Glowing amber-orange sky with a soft low sun just above a calm grey-green sea horizon (~62% down); thin warm clouds at top. Almost no detail, ideal behind lyrics: text sits anywhere, best in the upper two-thirds or over the sea. Titled sunset but reads as a dawn glow. Original 3811x2597.

assets.name: Pompton Plains, New Jersey — Jasper Francis Cropsey (The Met, CC0).webp
assets.notes: Wide valley in warm hazy autumn light: soft golden sky with light shafts takes the top ~55%, low blue hills and a silver river across the middle, golden fields below. Calm and low-detail; big empty sky for lyrics. Crop of 0.96 removes the unpainted canvas edge; artist's signature at bottom-left is mostly cropped by 16:9. Original 3811x2380.

assets.name: Twilight on the Sound, Darien, Connecticut — John Frederick Kensett (The Met, CC0).webp

credit.title: Twilight on the Sound, Darien, Connecticut
credit.creator: John Frederick Kensett

assets.notes: Still water at dusk: pale grey-green sky fading to a rose-pink horizon, pink reflections on glassy water, dark tree mass on the right third, a tiny rowing boat lower centre. Upper half and left side are empty for text. Wide 2.2:1 original (2777x1272) so the 16:9 crop trims the sides only; output slightly upscaled from ~2260 px wide, fine because the paint is soft.

assets.name: Sunrise — George Inness (The Met, CC0).webp
assets.notes: Tonalist, soft-focus meadow at sunrise: olive-gold haze, two thin trees (centre-left and right), a small figure in the field, warm light behind. Very low contrast and soft, so it works like a warm texture behind notice text (needs the dark gradient for legibility). Original 3917x2602.

assets.notes: 1920x1080 AV1, 29.97 fps, 148 s, one locked-off shot (no cuts found). Two fireworks clusters burst left and right; the silhouette of the Marine Corps War Memorial (Iwo Jima statue) with its flag sits low in the centre, with dark trees at the bottom. 76-92 s is the busiest, most colourful part (pink, blue, green, white bursts in drifting magenta smoke). Burst-free night sky at top for text. Designers should know the memorial silhouette is in frame.

assets.name: Eine kleine Nachtmusik, I. Allegro — Mozart, Nicolas Lambinon Quartet, 1923 (Internet Archive, PD).m4a

credit.title: Eine kleine Nachtmusik, K. 525: I. Allegro
credit.creator: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart (composer); Nicolas Lambinon String Quartet
credit.year: Recorded c. Nov 1923, Berlin; Odeon AA 79467, issued before July 1924
credit.basis: Composition: Mozart died 1791. Recording: first published 1924 (the label shows 1925 at the latest); US sound recordings published before 1926 are in the public domain (100-year term under the Music Modernization Act).

assets.notes: COMPROMISE, please review: a historic acoustic 78 rpm transfer, mono, frequency range up to about 3 kHz, with light surface noise; it sounds charmingly vintage, not hi-fi. I found no PD/CC0 modern recording: the PD-tagged Commons files ("European Archive"/Musopen) are only PD under EU law, and no US military band recording turned up. The Allegro fills 1.5-213 s of this side; the excerpt 1.5-101.5 s covers the exposition and early development and fades out over 4 s. Suits a 'through the years' nostalgia slideshow.

assets.name: Happy Birthday to You — synthesized arrangement by Pracchia-78 (Wikimedia Commons, PD).m4a

credit.title: Happy Birthday to You
credit.creator: Mildred J. Hill & Patty Hill (melody); arranged and rendered by Wikimedia user Pracchia-78
credit.basis: Song is public domain (melody 1893; US court ruled in 2016 that no valid copyright covered the lyrics); the recording was released into the public domain by its maker (Commons: Public domain, own work).

assets.notes: Instrumental, made in a software synthesizer with SoundFonts (a 'solo voices' patch plus reverb), stereo 44.1 kHz. The tune is played several times over about 75 s of music, steady level, natural tail at the end. It is pleasant but clearly synthetic, not a live band; I found no PD US military band recording that can be downloaded with curl (DVIDS blocks it).

assets.name: Maple Leaf Rag — Scott Joplin, 1916 piano roll (Wikimedia Commons, PD).m4a

credit.title: Maple Leaf Rag (piano roll, Aeolian/Uni-Record 202705)
credit.creator: Scott Joplin (composer and performer)
credit.basis: Composition published 1899 and Joplin died 1917; the piano roll was published in 1916 (before 1926), so PD in the US; this file is a mechanical audio rendering of a scan of that roll (no new creative authorship). Commons tags it Public domain.

assets.notes: Joplin's own piano-roll performance, clean modern piano sound (rendered from a roll scan, no surface noise), bright and bouncy, steady level throughout (~-24 dB RMS). Starts immediately (0.28 s lead-in). 90 s covers the A, B and repeat strains; fade out at the end. Alternative already downloaded: the 1906 US Marine Band 78 (File:1906 - Scott Joplin's Maple Leaf Rag (1899) played by the United States Marine Band.ogg, PD) - more period character but scratchy acoustic recording.

assets.name: Clock, ticking — natalie (PDSounds via Wikimedia Commons, PD).m4a

credit.title: Clock, ticking
credit.creator: natalie (PDSounds)
credit.basis: Released into the public domain by the author on PDSounds (pdsounds.org record 216); Commons tags it Public domain.

assets.notes: Crisp, big clockwork tick exactly once per second (transients at 0.10, 1.10, 2.10 ... s). The 0.05-4.05 s window holds exactly four ticks with matching gaps, so it loops seamlessly for a countdown; no fades on purpose.

assets.name: Typewriter ding — _stubb (Freesound via Wikimedia Commons, CC0).m4a
assets.notes: A single clean, bright bell 'ding' (pure tone with a few harmonics, quick decay), about 0.6 s of sound. Reads as a classic 'correct!' ding. Could be layered/doubled for a ding-ding.

assets.name: Buzzer — David Pride (Wikimedia Commons, CC0).m4a
assets.notes: A harsh, low, electronic game-show style 'wrong answer' buzz, constant for 1.5 s with a hard stop. Loud and rich in harmonics; may want -6 dB in the mix.

credit.title: Jubilant Fanfare
credit.creator: United States Navy Band (Ceremonial Band)
credit.basis: US federal government work: recording by the United States Navy Band (17 USC 105).

assets.notes: Brass and percussion fanfare. Alternatives: Ceremonial Fanfare (USAF Heritage of America Band, PD) and CC0 concert-hall applause (File:277021 sandermotions applause-2.wav, 6.3 s), both already in the local sfx folder.

assets.name: Wivenhoe Park, Essex — John Constable (National Gallery of Art, CC0).webp

credit.title: Wivenhoe Park, Essex
credit.creator: John Constable
credit.source: National Gallery of Art, Washington (via Wikimedia Commons)

assets.notes: Sunny English parkland: a bright green sloping meadow with black-and-white cows and a rustic wooden fence in the foreground (lower left), a calm lake with swans and a rowing boat across the middle, a dark band of trees and a red-brick house beyond, and a huge billowing white-cloud blue sky filling the top 45%. Very wide original (4000x2160, 1.85:1) so the 16:9 crop only trims the sides. Sky is the natural place for a title; it is busy with clouds, so use a bold storybook title with a shadow/plate.

assets.name: The Avenue at Middelharnis — Meindert Hobbema (Wikimedia Commons, PD).webp

credit.title: The Avenue at Middelharnis
credit.creator: Meindert Hobbema
credit.source: The National Gallery, London (photo via Wikimedia Commons)
credit.basis: PD-Art: faithful photograph of a 2D painting whose artist died in 1709.

assets.notes: The classic 'road into the distance': a straight, rutted sandy lane runs from the bottom centre to a vanishing point in the middle, lined by two rows of very tall, thin, bare-trunked poplars; a man with a dog walks up it. Village church tower on the left horizon, red-roofed farm on the right, a tree nursery in the right foreground. Large soft blue sky with a white cumulus at right. Strong one-point perspective - perfect start line for the race. Crop keeps the foreground road (offset 0.85) and trims a little of the sky; poplar tops still in frame. Upper-left sky is the calmest space for text. Cooler, greyer greens than the other backdrops.

assets.name: A Summer Afternoon — Asher Brown Durand (Wikimedia Commons, PD).webp

credit.title: A Summer Afternoon
credit.creator: Asher Brown Durand
credit.basis: PD-Art: faithful photograph of a 2D painting whose artist died in 1886.

assets.notes: Warm, drowsy afternoon: a great spreading elm/oak with a thick trunk right of centre throws deep shade over a grassy bank where cows and sheep drink at a shallow stream; one cow lies resting in the shade (lower right) - ideal for the hare's nap. Lighter woodland and a hazy sunlit valley at left, pale cream-blue sky upper left (the empty area for text). Rich golden-greens. The 16:9 crop (offset 0.8) keeps the animals and stream and trims some sky.

assets.name: Peace and Plenty — George Inness (The Met, CC0).webp
assets.notes: Golden sunset over a wide harvest valley: an amber-and-rose evening sky across the top half, two big dark trees silhouetted left of centre, a river glinting in the middle distance, rolling hills behind, and stooks of harvested wheat with tiny harvesters in the warm foreground. Celebratory, end-of-day mood for the finish and curtain call. The original is quite dark and brownish, so the process adds a gentle lift (brightness/contrast/saturation/gamma); the sky (top 40%) is the space for 'The End' / cast names. If you want something brighter and greener, an alternative is Thomas Cole's 'View from Mount Holyoke (The Oxbow)', Met 10497, CC0, a literal hilltop view (already downloaded at a/cand/oxbow.jpg).

assets.name: Young Hare — Albrecht Dürer (Albertina via Google Arts & Culture, PD).webp

credit.title: Young Hare (Feldhase)
credit.creator: Albrecht Dürer
credit.source: Albertina, Vienna (Google Arts & Culture, via Wikimedia Commons)
credit.basis: PD-Art: faithful photograph of a 2D watercolour whose artist died in 1528.

assets.notes: The famous watercolour: a crouching brown hare facing three-quarters right, ears up, every hair painted, on a plain cream paper ground with a soft shadow to the right; Dürer's 1502 date and AD monogram below. Portrait (3731x4123, almost square). Kept whole (no crop); the cream background is not transparent, so present it as a framed 'portrait card' on the stage rather than cut-out.

assets.name: Testudo carbonaria — J. de C. Sowerby & Edward Lear (Biodiversity Heritage Library, PD).webp

credit.title: Testudo carbonaria (red-footed tortoise), plate from Thomas Bell, A Monograph of the Testudinata
credit.creator: James de Carle Sowerby (drawing) and Edward Lear (lithograph); printed by C. Hullmandel
credit.source: Smithsonian Libraries / Biodiversity Heritage Library (Internet Archive)
credit.basis: Published in London 1832-36; artists died 1871 (Sowerby) and 1888 (Lear).

assets.notes: Hand-coloured lithograph of a red-footed tortoise striding to the right, head up with a bright eye, glossy black domed shell with golden-yellow scute patches, yellow-spotted legs, a tuft of grey grass behind its head, on a pale cream paper ground. Charming and friendly - a natural 'hero' for the race, and walking toward the finish (right). The process crops the full book page (3415x4895) to the animal with a margin of paper all round (whole tortoise kept, caption and page edges dropped), giving ~1.55:1. The scan is a moderately compressed JPEG; fine at <=1920 px but do not enlarge further.

assets.name: Morning Mood (Peer Gynt) — Edvard Grieg, Musopen Symphony (Wikimedia Commons, PD).m4a

credit.title: Peer Gynt Suite No. 1, Op. 46 - I. Morning Mood
credit.creator: Edvard Grieg (composer); Musopen Symphony Orchestra (Czech National Symphony Orchestra)
credit.basis: Composition: Grieg died 1907. Recording: made for Musopen's Kickstarter project and released into the public domain by Musopen; Commons tags it Public domain.

assets.notes: Full orchestra, clean modern studio sound. 0-45 s: the flute/oboe sunrise theme passing back and forth; 45-75 s: the warm full-orchestra sunrise climax (loudest); 75-90 s settles down, fade out 4 s. Perfect for the meadow opening.

assets.name: William Tell Overture (finale) — Gioachino Rossini, United States Marine Band (Wikimedia Commons, PD).m4a

credit.title: William Tell Overture (transcr. Wenzel Sedlak), from Grand Scenes
credit.creator: Gioachino Rossini (composer); United States Marine Band, Timothy Foley (director)
credit.source: United States Marine Band via Wikimedia Commons
credit.basis: Composition: Rossini died 1868, Sedlak transcription 19th century. Recording: US federal government work by the United States Marine Band (17 USC 105).

assets.notes: Wind-band version of the famous finale. The excerpt begins at 7:31 with the trumpet call that ends the Ranz des vaches (about 11 s), then the galloping 'Lone Ranger' galop from ~7:43 onward; 85 s of non-stop racing energy, fade out 3 s. Level is moderate (band recording, ~-32 dB RMS); normalise if needed.

assets.name: Referee whistle blow — SpliceSound (Freesound via Wikimedia Commons, CC0).m4a
assets.notes: One sharp, short pea-whistle blast (~0.5 s, starts at 0.09 s) with a natural gym-hall reverb tail; trimmed to 1.8 s with a short fade. 'Ready, steady... go!' start signal.
